Typography

Editorial serif typography for headings, questions and concepts. Clean, readable sans-serif for controls and supporting information.

Interaction principles

- Icon-only action buttons. The accessible name carries the meaning. A tooltip explains a less familiar action when a pointer can hover.
- Navigation links, text links, headings, field labels, and explanatory text keep their words.
- Horizontal carousels with the next card deliberately peeking into view.
- Generous spacing, but good use of available mobile screen space.
- Soft card borders and rounded corners.
- Coral for emphasis, not decoration everywhere.
- Botanical imagery to reinforce the idea of curiosity growing.

## Colour

The swatches above are the brand. The app also has a few near-duplicates. Use one token for each role. Do not add another orange or another ink.

| Role | Token | Where it already appears |
|---|---|---|
| Paper, page ground | `#F5F1EA` | `studio-cream`, the page behind every surface |
| Paper, card | `#FFFAF3` | `studio-paper`, panels lifted off the ground |
| Coral | `#FF7F50` | The named brand coral, and the banner (`logo-orange`) |
| Deep teal | `#182326` | `studio-ink`, text and the dark plant field |
| Stone | `#D8D0C2` | `studio-line`, card and field borders |
| Botanical green | `#47715C` | `studio-grove`, the green of growth, not a second accent for buttons |

`#F4EFE6` in the swatch and `#F5F1EA` on the page are the same paper family. Keep the page colour that is already on screen. `#182627` in the swatch and `#182326` in the app are the same deep teal. Keep `#182326`.

`studio-coral` is `#FF7F50`, the same coral as the banner. The hover step remains `#FF907C`. Coral is the accent, the selected state, and an important confirmation. It is not the ground of every action. Quiet actions stay outlined. A strong confirm that is not the coral confirmation uses deep teal.

`#FF7F50` is the accent colour. It is for fills, rings, selected states, and the banner. It is not a text colour on cream or paper: as text on `#F5F1EA` it is about 2.2:1. Text that should still read as coral uses `studio-coral-text`, `#B8472A`. That is the darker coral for words. Buttons, focus rings, and the countdown ring stay `#FF7F50`.

Eyebrow labels, chip labels, and the garden date line use `#656D69` (`studio-eyebrow`, `studio-label`, `studio-date`). Muted metadata and the garden footer use `#686E6A` (`studio-muted`, `studio-footer`). Sidebar hints use `#5B615D` (`studio-note`), which is darker because the sidebar ground is darker than the page. Body text stays `#45524F`.

Botanical green `#47715C` stays `studio-grove` for growth on cream, paper, and the soft mint notice. Words set directly on the mint card `#A8D6C1` use `studio-grove-text`, `#375848`.

Text on the page meets WCAG AA: 4.5:1 for normal text, and 3:1 for large text (24px, or 18.66px bold). These text colours clear 4.5:1 on the ground they sit on, so the large headings clear 3:1 as well. Do not fix a failing colour by painting the words deep teal, and do not replace the brand coral fill with the text coral.

Violet appears only as a shelf dot. It is not a button colour.

## Typography

Headings, questions, concept titles, and the represented question use the serif. Controls, labels, hints, and body explanation use the sans.

The serif in the app is Georgia. Keep it. It is already the editorial voice on every screen, and it does not need a downloaded face.

The sans is `system-ui, "Segoe UI", sans-serif`. Georgia remains the serif. Do not load a new webfont for this pass.

| Use | Face | Size |
|---|---|---|
| Surface heading | Serif | 36px, tightening to 48px from the small breakpoint |
| Section heading | Serif | 24px |
| Question or concept title | Serif | 20–24px |
| Eyebrow | Mono, uppercase, tracked | 10px |
| Body and labels | Sans | 14–16px |
| Field text | Sans | 16px, so a phone does not zoom the field |

Do not set interface labels below 14px. Garden chips use 14px for the question and 10px for the kind eyebrow.

## Spacing

Use an 8px step, with 4px only for tight icon padding.

| Step | Use |
|---|---|
| 4 | Gap inside an icon button |
| 8 | Related icon buttons in a row |
| 12 | Card stacks on a phone, the peek gap in a carousel |
| 16 | Field padding, page padding on a phone |
| 24 | Card padding on a phone |
| 32 | Card padding from the small breakpoint, space between sections |
| 40 | A major break between regions |
| 48 | Desktop column gap where a section needs air |

## Cards and fields

| Piece | Radius | Border | Padding |
|---|---|---|---|
| Panel | 24px | 1px stone | 24px, 32px from the small breakpoint |
| Artwork frame | 24px | none, or 1px stone when it needs an edge | the image fills the frame |
| Field | 16px | 1px stone | 12px 16px |
| Icon button | 12px | see treatments below | the target is the padding |

Shared panels use a 24px corner. Compare artwork frames use the same 24px corner. Question cards were already 24px. Screens that still use a 28px frame keep it until that screen is touched. Do not square the corners, and do not go larger than 24px for new work.

## Buttons and icons

An action button contains an icon and no visible word. Navigation links and text links keep their words, even when a link is drawn with a quiet outline.

Use Lucide, the set already in the app. One family, one stroke. The glyph is 18px. Do not mix 14, 15, and 16 in new work.

Every action button is at least 44 by 44 pixels. The current quiet icon control is 40. Bring it to 44 with the other controls.

| Treatment | Ground | Icon | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| Primary | Coral `#FF7F50` | Deep teal | The one commit on that view: plant, save, begin |
| Secondary | Deep teal | Ivory `#FFF8ED` | A strong confirm that is not the coral commit |
| Quiet | Transparent, 1px stone border | Deep teal | Park, discard, restore, cancel, replace, and the other local actions |

States:

- Hover, pointer only: primary moves to `#FF907C`. Quiet and secondary use the existing sidebar hover `#E2DACE` as a wash behind the icon.
- Focus: a 2px coral outline, 2px outside the control. This is the focus already used in the app.
- Selected: coral ground and deep teal icon, as the chosen image and the chosen image count already do.
- Disabled: 40% opacity. The control stays in place. It does not disappear.

The accessible name is required. It names the action and, when the target matters, the thing it acts on. Example: “Discard this question”, not “Discard”.

A tooltip is for a pointer that can hover, and for keyboard focus. It repeats the accessible name in plain language. Do not use a `title` attribute as the only explanation. A `title` attribute does not show on touch. On a phone, the heading, the field label, or the card itself is the context. If that context is not enough, the action is ambiguous and needs a better icon or a text link, not words inside the button.

While an action is working, the button stays an icon. The progress sentence sits beside it, as the screen already does for “Saving the image…”.

## Layout

Mobile is the 375px-wide phone. The heading, the action, and the first card should fit without a second navigation and without a control wrapping onto a stray line. Sections stack. Icon actions that belong to one task stay together on a single row. They do not wrap, and the last icon is not left on a row of its own. Numbered choices, such as 1, 2, and 4 images, are a complete group. On a phone that group sits on the next row. From the small breakpoint it can sit beside the icons, still as one group.

A long optional checklist, such as related questions when saving a concept, may be closed inside a disclosure. The summary keeps its words, including that the list is optional. Opening it does not save anything. The commit action stays outside the disclosure.

Desktop is the same surfaces with more room. From the large breakpoint, navigation can sit in a side column and the botanical mark can move there with it. Do not invent a dashboard, a gauge, or a dense toolbar.

The sidebar currently starts at one breakpoint and the question carousel stays horizontal until a wider one. When layout is next touched, use one width for that change so a tablet is not a side column and a sideways list at the same time.

## Horizontal carousels

A horizontal carousel is a feature. The next card is partly visible so the row invites a swipe. A cut-off card is not overflow to be fixed.

Question lists use a native snap row. Each card is about 82% of the row, with a 12px gap, so the next card peeks. Swipe, scroll, and snap stay.

The Library keeps the current concept large and places the neighbours beside it, smaller. Swipe moves between concepts. Do not replace either carousel with a vertical list.

Candidate images may stay one image wide on a phone. On a wide screen they may show a sliver of the next image, in the same spirit. They do not become a grid.

Prompt, accept, and generate on Visualise use `IconAction`. Keep `Bot`, `Check`, and `ImagePlus`. Their names stay “Ask for an image prompt”, “Accept this prompt”, and “Generate 1 image” or “Generate N images”. Asking and generating are quiet. Accepting the prompt is deep teal. Saving the concept is the coral confirmation. A chosen image count, and the chosen image, use coral as the selected state.

Garden uses the same control. Planting is the coral sprout. Saving a correction is deep teal. The other garden actions are quiet. Park and discard sit under “Manage this question”, with a sentence beside them. An empty garden’s three invitations keep their words. Choosing one places the cursor in the planting field. It does not create a question.

Library uses the same control. Comparing concepts is quiet and sits beside the scope. Editing a concept is quiet. Saving those changes is the coral confirmation. Cancelling the edit is quiet. On a phone the botanical tree follows the concept, so the artwork stays in front.

Home uses the same control. Beginning a curiosity is the coral sprout. Saving a renamed curiosity is deep teal, as is replacing its cover. The other home actions are quiet. Library of Curiosities stays a text link. On a wide screen the dictionary and the invitation sit side by side, and the curiosity cards sit in two columns. A phone keeps them in one column.

These keep their words:

- Home, Garden, Visualise, and Library in the shell.
- Library of Curiosities on the curiosity home.
- View in the library, Return to the garden, Return to your curiosities, and Back to the library.
- Correct the capture, Hide from this comparison, and Read full question. These are text links.
- The 1, 2, and 4 image choices. The number is the choice, not an action word.
- A suggested title. The words are the title being offered.

Ambiguous icons, and the context that keeps words out of the button:

- `Sprout` is used for Begin, Plant, and Turn into a question. Each form already has its own heading or field label. The tooltip names which planting it is.
- Restore and Restore as its own question must not share one icon. `RotateCcw` returns a parked or discarded question. `Undo2` separates a merged wording. The merged-wording sentence stays beside `Undo2`.
- Replace left and Replace right use the same icon. Put each control under its own image. The accessible name says which side.
- `Check` means accept the prompt on Visualise, and save an edit elsewhere. Those screens are not open together. Save concept uses `Bookmark`, not `Check`, so it is not the prompt tick.
- `Trash2` is both Discard and Remove image. Discard sits on the question. Remove image sits in the cover dialog under the heading Cover image.
- `Image` on a question card means Visualise. `ImagePlus` means generate images, or add a cover. They are not on the same card.
- `X` is every cancel and close. The open field or dialog is the context. The accessible name says which one is closing.
